summary: A (category, year) pair counts as settled only once its walk reached a terminator with nothing failing, and a terminator write now truncates stale rows past it.
reason: settledPairs selected any pair having a 'found' page, so a pair whose walk was cut short -- by a mid-page transport error, or by exhausting --max-scan-pages -- was indistinguishable from a completed one. Every later run then SKIPPED it, printing 'every requested (category, year) pair is already settled; nothing to probe' and making zero requests, so the rest of that category/year was permanently absent from the corpus. --strict could not catch it because loadCoverage accumulated 'settled' with the same predicate, making PairsRemaining 0 and exiting 0 on an incomplete corpus. Downstream has no completeness gate, so a rename or suspension notice on an unfetched page reads as 'does not exist' rather than 'not fetched' -- the exact liar-map this command exists to prevent. Both terminator paths already wrote 'not-found-at-source', so requiring one is what separates a finished walk from an abandoned one. The truncation is required to avoid trading the skip bug for a permanent-RESCAN bug: upsertBucket can only overwrite a row at the same page, so a stale error row at a page beyond a later, shorter walk's terminator would keep the pair unsettled forever.
validated_outcome: Four regression tests reproduce the original defect mechanically: a pair with a failed page 2 and a pair truncated at the scan bound are both refused as settled, a clean terminator still settles, a stale error row past a terminator no longer blocks settling, and loadCoverage now reports the same settled set as the probe path plus a separate pairs_partially_walked counter.
